title: Decouple and Decompose: Scaling Resource Allocation with DeDe
problem: Resource allocation optimization in cloud systems has grown beyond the capacity of commercial solvers as problem scale increases. Existing approaches either specialize in narrow domains or impose workload-specific assumptions that limit generalizability.
motivation: Efficient resource allocation is critical in cloud systems to enable resource sharing among multiple tenants.
method: DeDe starts by recognizing that resource allocation problems (the challenge of distributing resources to meet competing demands) have a natural separation: the constraints governing resources are independent from the constraints governing demands. It breaks the optimization into alternating subproblems for each resource and each demand, which can be solved both efficiently and in parallel. The framework is provided as a Python package with an intuitive modeling interface.
key_novelty: The key insight is that resource and demand constraints in allocation problems are naturally separable, making it possible to decompose them into parallelizable subproblems.
contributions: Structural analysis revealing separability in real-world resource allocation problems
DeDe framework with decouple-and-decompose strategy for scalable resource allocation
Open-source Python implementation with standard modeling interface
Empirical validation on cluster scheduling, traffic engineering, and load balancing showing significant speedups and improved solution quality

metrics.speedup: significant improvement across cluster scheduling, traffic engineering, and load balancing tasks

primary_theme: scalable distributed optimization for resource allocation
